transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. Um, the main reason I’m here is that I'm having a lot of trouble at work. I'm a health services manager, and lately, anything that takes real, sitting-down brain work... it just feels like I hit a wall. 

Like doing the monthly reports, or trying to plan out a multi-site health event. I just keep putting it off, even when I know it really matters and needs to get done. It's just getting really frustrating.
Have you noticed that you're not enjoying things at work or outside of work that you usually find enjoyable?

No, not really. I mean, I still enjoy my downtime and my hobbies just fine. Outside of work, things are pretty normal... I still like doing the things I've always liked. 

It's really just getting myself to sit down and do those heavy mental tasks at the clinic that's the issue. I don't feel like I've lost interest in life or anything like that.
Do you find yourself feeling unusually anxious, worried, or on edge when you're faced with tasks that require a lot of mental effort at work?

Not really, no. I don't feel anxious or worried about the tasks themselves. It's not like I'm on edge or scared to do the reports. Um... it's really just that I can't seem to make myself start them. So, no, I wouldn't say anxiety is the issue.
When you try to do these mentally demanding tasks at work, do you feel unusually fatigued or like you don't have the energy to get through them?

No, it's not a physical tiredness. I don't feel fatigued or like I'm out of energy. I have the energy to do other things around the clinic just fine. It's just... when it comes to those specific tasks, it's like my brain just won't engage with them. But I wouldn't say I feel physically exhausted or anything.

When you think about those mentally demanding tasks at work, do you feel any sense of pleasure or satisfaction when you complete them, or does it feel like there's no reward or motivation to push through them?

I definitely feel satisfied when they're finally done. It's a big relief to get them off my desk, actually. So, yeah, I do feel a sense of accomplishment once it's over. The problem isn't how I feel at the end... it's really just getting myself to start and actually push through the work itself.
Have you noticed any difficulty starting or following through with tasks or activities when you're at home or in other settings outside of work?

Not really, no. Um... when I'm at home, I don't seem to have that same problem. If there's yard work or stuff to fix around the house, I usually just tackle it without much of an issue. It really just seems to be tied to those specific types of tasks at the clinic.
Looking back, were you often distracted, had trouble focusing, or struggled to finish tasks even as a child, or is this something that's developed more recently?

No, it's definitely been around since I was a kid. Um... even back in elementary school, my teachers would always tell my parents that I was bright, but that I was just constantly daydreaming. I was always losing my worksheets, too. Honestly, I would forget to turn in my homework entirely unless my mom actually went through my backpack every single night to check it. So, yeah, it's not a new thing at all.
Have you ever noticed similar difficulties focusing or finishing tasks in other areas of your life, like at school, at home, or with personal projects, even if it wasn't work-related?

Well, like I said, at home with chores and stuff, I do okay. But... it does bleed into other things, yeah. I mean, I'm still getting by overall, at work and just out in the community, but it's not without problems. People have had to cover gaps for me because I just couldn't get things together in time. Deadlines have definitely slipped. And... honestly, it's embarrassing. I've had to make a lot of last-minute apologies to my coworkers, and even to friends when I drop the ball on personal stuff we planned. So it does affect my life, even if I manage to keep my head above water.
